title: Reflections and a hidden root
stem: For $0≤x≤2\pi$ define $F(x)=\sin x+\sin(\pi-x)+\cos x-\cos(\pi-x)$. Work without a calculator. The diagram illustrates the reflection for a point P in the first quadrant.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Solve $F(x)=2$ exactly, retaining both endpoints where appropriate.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find all real $k$ such that $F(x)=k$ has exactly three distinct solutions on the stated closed interval. Justify completeness.

steps.text: Reflection across the vertical axis preserves the sine coordinate.
On a half-open period every interior ordinate is taken twice, with just one root at an extremum.
Closing the interval adds a second endpoint only at the ordinate $F(0)=2$.

title: Which transformations preserve a trigonometric equation?
stem: Let $g(x)=\sin^2x-\cos^2x$ for real $x$. Work without a calculator.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Solve $g(x)=1/2$ on $0≤x<2\pi$. A student argues that shifting each solution by $\pi/2$ supplies four more. Evaluate the argument.

steps.text: Under the first reflection the cosine changes sign but both squares are unchanged.
Under the shift the sine and cosine squares exchange roles.
The shift maps these to solutions of $g(x)=-1/2$, so it adds none.
